Four-surface package contract — each file answers exactly one question
Deliberate redundancy — template prompts live in BOTH the skill and the trainee material; never deduplicate
Rules are re-sent on every message (~34KB before the trainee types); @import does not help
Skills are the lazy-loading mechanism — only the description sits in context, the body loads on demand
Per-message context budget stays flat (~20-26KB) as new playbooks are added
Day-1 bootstrap — on any opening message Claude introduces itself, detects the day, and starts guiding
Progress ledger in the package CLAUDE.md — first source for day detection
Task-based restructure — tasks are vertical slices carrying their own steps, conversation, turn and review
Section-scoped task IDs (task X.N) rather than a global counter
Rejected: global flat task numbering and 8.1.1-style child IDs
Trainer examples show product-building only — exclude bootcamp-authoring and trainer-stack content
Clause-level excerpting — excluding the D-numbered prompts is necessary but not sufficient
Never name internal or graded docs inside trainee-facing material
Ground every section in the sources, not memory — re-read the history before writing
Golden rule: the trainee supplies raw notes, Claude drafts the formal artifact, then review and refine
Trainee never reads or writes code — review by using the UI plus Claude's plain report
Testing is Claude's job — the trainee only triggers it and reads the non-technical report
Three testing layers per built function — automated re-runnable cases, server/CLI checks, chrome-devtools browser run
Every plan opens with a jargon-free 'what we'll build now' summary; technical detail sits after it
Default trainee stack — one full-stack Next.js app in app/, Supabase (Postgres + auth), Vercel, no Docker
Password-hashing rule — Claude always hashes; the trainer only verifies it happened
Server lifecycle rule — Claude starts servers for testing and explicitly stops them (no 'port occupied')
Secret hygiene — a pasted key goes into the command or .env only, and is logged as a placeholder
Arabic-ized formal keywords (EARS, Gherkin, JOURNEY/ACTOR/DECISION) for register consistency
Trainee register — simple local-leaning Arabic, each term defined once, no deep-technical vocabulary
Self-contained requirement — EARS plus user story plus acceptance plus tags together; tables are index-only
Independent QA time audit — 2,382 estimated minutes against 2,150 capacity, with per-day verdicts
Decision A-1 — scaffold runs on Day 1, live URL on Day 3; never two consecutive days without something running
Decision B — proposed content cuts; only B-3 accepted (scope folded into section 8), B-1/B-2/B-4 rejected
Scope folded into section 8 and everything renumbered — self-healing refs and anchor collisions handled
Anchor verification via github-slugger rules — grew from 86 to 298 links, 0 broken
Duplication check — no step text may appear both in a task's steps and its trainer collapsible
Contamination check — scan collapsibles for bootcamp-meta terms before shipping a section
Quote authenticity and cross-section reuse checks — every excerpt traces to a real non-D prompt, used once
215 working minutes per day (4 hours including the 25-minute break) — our division is canonical over the brochure
Session ranges instead of rigid blocks (45 / 59 / 85 / 26 average) plus continuous circulating review
DesignSync boundary — the design system syncs natively, generated screens do not (project type is immutable)
Copy Claude Design form answers back to Claude Code — and Claude must ask for them rather than wait
Page handoff hybrid — share the URL by default, download the page files on three named signals
ERD empty-boxes incident — a diagram can be structurally sound and still missing its content
Redraw the ERD from the real tables once they exist — a diagram that disagrees with reality is worse than none
Double-booking across two services of one provider — the case that defines integration testing
Attempt, do not assert — a security report must state attempts and outcomes, never a claim that permissions work
Automated-tests gap — the reference project never wrote per-functionality tests; the gap is why the rule exists
Deploy gap — the reference project deployed only at the very end and that session did not complete
Vercel MCP + CLI hybrid — MCP manages and reads logs, CLI does login/link/env/deploy (MCP has no env-var tools)
The five real Vercel obstacles pre-smoothed for trainees; the browser login confirmation is their only step
context7 setup — API key from context7.com, remote HTTP server added by Claude at user scope
Supabase setup — create the project first (save the DB password), then OAuth MCP at project scope
Deck decision — one self-contained dual-mode HTML file (present / reference), RTL-native and offline
DOCX RTL fix — run-level rtl marks, section-level bidi, per-run proofing language
SAG brochure alignment audit M1-M8 — closed with our day division declared canonical
Section 17 takes no tasks — it records rather than produces; a forced task would be busywork
Tool-registration rule — any new tool/MCP/skill goes into both CLAUDE.md and the tools table
The 29-row task map (task / executor / day) — one lookup instead of scanning ten day blocks
Richer executor labels (trainee 10, Claude 15, Claude Design 2, Claude Code 1, draw.io 1) over a binary split
The trainee pastes keys into chat and Claude writes .env — never hand-edits project files
Push cadence — end of every functionality iteration AND end of day, docs included, repo exists from Day 1
Per-feature cycle — pull that piece's design, build it wired to the DB, test it, try it, push
Section 15 is the final integration pass — 14 asks 'does this piece work alone', 15 'does it all still work together'
Teach each integration the day it is first connected, not all of them on Day 1
Record gaps honestly instead of inventing prompts — the absence itself becomes the lesson
Categorize future work, never build it — the future-plan list stays, the work does not happen
Antigravity IDE (Standalone) — installed on Day 1, hosts the Claude Code extension
Claude Desktop app — installed on Day 1 to check the 5-hour and weekly usage limits
Vercel MCP (mcp.vercel.com) — hosted OAuth MCP for deploy management and log reading
Supabase MCP — OAuth, no personal access token; connected Day 1 because login must work Day 1
context7 MCP — current library docs, connected before anything code-related
chrome-devtools MCP — Claude's browser testing layer, connected at task 14.2
Claude Design + Design System + DesignSync — the section-12 design toolchain
